data.why: A microwave oven stands cut open on a cart in a kitchen with a cold mug on its turntable and a hand at its start button; the waves are followed from the magnetron into the cavity, onto the mug and out at the door, and the heat they leave in the magnetron to its fan. The camera opens close on the mug under the waves, frames each part as it is added, and ends on the hand pressing start and the mug steaming.

recurring.what: a hand at the start button

chain.shows: one side of the mug glows hot while the rest stays cold
the waves leak out of the open front past the spinning turntable
chain.stakes: the kitchen is hit by waves

chain.shows: the door swings open mid-cook and waves leak at the hand
with the latch switch letting power back on, the magnetron glows red hot
kept cool by the fan, it never stops and the mug boils over

surprises.claim: Microwaves bounce around inside the oven and form hot and cold spots, which is why most ovens have a turntable.
surprises.search: microwave oven standing waves hot spots turntable why

surprises.claim: The metal mesh in a microwave's door has holes much smaller than the microwaves' wavelength of about 12 centimeters, so the waves cannot pass through.
surprises.search: microwave door mesh holes smaller than wavelength 12 cm Faraday cage

surprises.claim: Microwave ovens have interlock switches that cut power to the magnetron as soon as the door opens.
surprises.search: microwave oven door interlock switches cut power magnetron when door opens

ideas.idea: waves aimed at a cold mug is a microwave
the waves bounce into hot spots and half the mug stays cold
a turntable carries the mug through the hot spots
the waves leak out of the open front
a door with a metal mesh blocks them
opening that door mid-cook lets waves out at your hand
a switch in the door latch cuts the power
a fan blows cool air across it
the mug keeps cooking until it boils over
a timer switches the waves off
press start and the mug comes out steaming

sentences.text: If you aim invisible waves at a cold mug, you have a microwave.
But the waves bounce into hot spots, and half stays cold.
So a turntable spins the mug through the spots.
But the waves leak out the open front.
So a door with metal mesh blocks them.
But open that door mid-cook, and waves hit your hand.
So a switch in the latch cuts the power.
But the hard-working magnetron gets burning hot.
So a fan blows cool air across it.
But the mug keeps cooking until it boils over.
So a timer switches the waves off.
Press start, and your mug comes out steaming.
